facts.note: The complete Meridian original explicitly states embedded execution and one local file; the exact quotation preserves both clauses.
The Meridian original states one writer at a time per database. The fact retains the per-database boundary.
The Meridian original permits continuing readers when journal mode is enabled. The fact preserves that stated condition without claiming it is the only possible mode.
The original explicitly places filesystem-locking validation before shared-filesystem use.
The original limits its suitability statement to one application instance and modest write traffic; the fact correctly attributes that statement to this fictional fixture.
The Boreal original explicitly describes a separate database service.
The concurrent-writer statement includes conflicting updates waiting or retrying. Both the capability and qualification survive.
The original expressly requires workload-specific tuning for connection limit and transaction behavior.
The original explicitly permits several application instances over the network; no numerical capacity is inferred.
The Meridian original warns an open-file copy can be incomplete and prescribes backup interface or stopped writes. The fact preserves the alternatives and qualification.
Both adjacent Meridian clauses concern this same embedded product: no server/network authentication and application/OS file-access responsibility. The conjunction is supported in context.
The Boreal original names access control and supported updates as operator responsibilities; the narrower fact is accurate.
The complete Boreal original requires scheduled backups and tested restores and states logical export availability; the fact does not infer failover from the export.
The original requires additional high-availability configuration and explicitly disclaims uninterrupted failover; the fact preserves that boundary.
The final Boreal paragraph expressly requires service monitoring and recovery ownership.
The Boreal source explicitly says no comparative throughput measurements or operating cost figures are supplied.
The Meridian source explicitly supplies no comparative throughput measurements. This is a fixture evidence limit, not a real product claim.

findings.note: The recommendation is conditional, grounded in single-instance/modest-write Meridian suitability and networked/multiwriter Boreal capability, with contention, tuning and shared-filesystem caveats preserved. The implication asks for the missing topology rather than declaring a winner.

The inference correctly separates removal of the separate service from backup/file-access duties. The Boreal duties, recovery recommendation and high-availability qualification are supported by the two complete fictional originals; actual recovery objectives remain unknown.

The complete sources supply no comparative throughput data and Boreal supplies no cost figures. They cannot establish a measured comparative winner. The workload-validation recommendation and no-benchmark/no-migration limitations are proportionate.

prose.note: Both originals explicitly identify invented products for a controlled test. The no-network/no-workload-test boundary is correctly presented as a limitation rather than evidence of capability.
Candidate recommendations retain the relevant topology, modest-write and contention/tuning conditions, without an unconditional product or performance winner.

Narrow the reader statement: the source says readers can continue WHEN journal mode is enabled, not ONLY WHEN. The added necessity/exclusivity claim is not established by the complete supplied source. Other clauses are supported. Remove only or obtain evidence establishing exclusivity.

The networked/multiwriter capability, potential waits/retries and tuning requirement are documented. Calling this a capability difference rather than measured throughput superiority is a sound inference given absent benchmarks.
The backup alternatives, incomplete open-copy risk, lack of exposed server and application/OS access responsibility all follow from Meridian’s complete original.
Boreal’s update/access/backup/restore/monitoring/recovery duties, logical export, extra HA configuration and no uninterrupted-failover promise remain within the supplied fixture.
No measured performance/cost winner is supported by these fictional materials; the text accurately states the missing comparative data.

The full supplied documents provide no application-specific instance count, workload conflicts, filesystem topology, recovery targets or restore results. The conditional information request is useful and not a fabricated fact.
The brief retains the report’s conditional candidate split, rather than an unsupported blanket recommendation.
The shared-filesystem, conflict/retry and workload-tuning qualifications are explicit in the original sources and correctly preserved.
The brief keeps the important inference: embedded does not eliminate backup/access work, while separate-service operational duties are specifically documented.
The open-file backup and HA/failover qualifications remain exact in meaning and useful to a downstream author.
The evidence-data limitation and resulting lack of a measured comparative winner are supported and preserved during shortening.

assessment.note: The report is a clear, purpose-shaped, conditional comparison covering deployment, concurrency, maintenance and evidence limits using the complete two fictional supplied documents. The brief prioritizes the decision and consequential caveats. Four logical source IDs represent two original documents and are not treated as four independent corroborations. Correct the unsupported ONLY WHEN necessity claim in concurrency:0 before completion. No public source, actual database, workload, migration, cost or cross-harness behavior was tested.
